display.purpose: The wordmark only; 62% width, black, italic, uppercase, magenta glow.

headline.purpose: Song title on the song page; balanced wrap.

title.purpose: Page titles, results title, Paused and Calibrate (up to clamp(3rem, 6vw, 4.6rem)).

score.purpose: Results score counting up; tabular figures. HUD score is clamp(50px, 3.2vw, 88px).

button.purpose: Buttons, risers, tabs, keycaps. Small 1rem, big 1.35rem.

label.purpose: Section labels, setlist heading, stat captions, pills and tags.

subhead.purpose: Artist line on the song page; normal width, upright.

body.purpose: Hints and errors; max 62ch; normal width, upright, sentence case.

body-strong.purpose: Setting names, checkbox labels, controller names.

rootFontSize.purpose: Every menu size is rem off this root so the interface grows for TV distance.

geometry.name: lean
geometry.purpose: Shared forward lean for every slab, thumb, checkbox, pip, meter, sheen, selection and wipe band.

shadows.name: spotlight-cone
shadows.purpose: Light falling on the focused control from above (background, not box-shadow).

shadows.name: selection-drop
shadows.purpose: Lit selection slab: white underline plus soft drop.

shadows.name: primary-lip
shadows.purpose: Darker base under a magenta button.

shadows.name: sleeve
shadows.purpose: Cover art in the setlist (song page: 0 30px 50px -24px).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for entrances, lifts, travel and wipes in.

motion.name: ease-bounce
motion.purpose: HUD break ring bounce on each bar (0.55s).

motion.name: focus-lift
motion.value: translateY(-3px) over 0.25s; spotlight fades in over 0.3s

motion.name: scene-forward
motion.purpose: Going deeper (setlist to song to results).

motion.name: cover-sheen
motion.purpose: Light band across a pointed or focused cover.

motion.name: launch-wipe
motion.value: three skewed bands (magenta, lit slab, ground) in 0.55s staggered 60ms; hold >= 620ms; out 0.5s

motion.name: results-reveal
motion.value: stars 0.55s from 250ms, 140ms apart; score count-up 1.3s; tags at 1.2s; stats from 0.85s, 45ms apart

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Drop entrances, staggers, sheen, bounce and travel; keep state changes; launch wipe becomes a fade; score shows final value.

feedback.sounds: Synthesized via Web Audio, own volume, not routed through music volume. move, select, back, tab, toggle-on, toggle-off, launch, star, count, best, pause, resume, error, add. Per-control choice via data-sfx (back, tab, launch, none). During play only the pause menu sounds.

rumble.name: tab-left / tab-right
rumble.value: amp 0.45, 40ms, click fully on the side moved toward

feedback.rumbleScope: Only on the controller last used, scaled by the rumble setting; native haptics on controllers that support them.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Song page to one column with a 9rem cover; result stats to two columns.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Settings to one column; part risers two by two; smaller HUD score and multiplier.

layout.hudUnits: px with vw clamps (sits over highway geometry)

narrative.overview:
The menus are the stage a player stands on between songs. The house lights are down to a deep indigo, a violet haze rises from the bottom of the screen, and every choice is a riser: a squared slab that leans forward with the type. The control that has focus is the one under the spotlight: it lifts a few pixels and a cyan light falls onto it. What the player has chosen is lit from inside and carries a white edge underneath, and when the choice changes that lit slab travels to the new item instead of blinking. The player's own cover art is the setlist and carries most of the colour on the library screen; the interface around it stays dark and inky so the covers and the single magenta action read first.

The type does the shouting. Archivo is set condensed, black and leaning italic for everything that is display, a control name or a number, and at normal width and upright for everything a player reads as a sentence. Nothing is rounded except the cover art corners (barely), tiny tags, and the round multiplier disc in the HUD. Density is couch-first: one primary column of decisions, large targets, and type sized in rem off a root that grows with the window so the same layout reads at a desk and from across a room.

Motion and feedback are physical but brief. Screens slide in from the side the player is heading, entrances stagger by tens of milliseconds, starting a song sweeps three stage-light bands across the screen, and every move and press has a synthesized sound and, on a controller, a matching rumble pulse. During play the menu world steps back: the HUD is quiet chrome around the highway, and nothing in it animates for decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Deep indigo ground with a violet haze field; ink tinted from the ground, never pure grey.
Squared slabs skewed forward by one shared lean angle (-9deg), matching the italic type.
Three light roles that never trade places: magenta acts, cyan focuses, a lit white-edged slab marks the selection.
Lane colours are data (part, difficulty, key binding, multiplier level), not decoration.
Condensed black italic Archivo for display, controls and numbers; normal-width upright Archivo for reading.
Rem sizing off a clamped root (16px to 26px) so the whole interface scales for TV distance.
Every interaction has sound; on a controller it also has a pulse. Reduced motion keeps state changes and drops travel.

rules.name: The Three Lights Rule
rules.body: Magenta acts, cyan focuses, a lit slab selects. Cyan never fills, never marks a choice and never decorates in a menu; a selected item is never magenta; focus and selection on the same item show both (lit slab plus cyan ring).

rules.name: The One Magenta Rule
rules.body: Each screen has at most one magenta button at rest, and it is the step forward (usually the one that starts music). Everything else is a slab or a ghost.

rules.name: The Lanes Are Data Rule
rules.body: A lane colour always means a lane, a difficulty level or a multiplier level. Never use one as a brand accent or a decorative stripe.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: If it is a name, a control or a number, set it condensed, black, italic and uppercase. If a player reads it as a sentence, set it at normal width, upright and in sentence case. Never set a sentence in the stage voice.

rules.name: The Couch Floor Rule
rules.body: The root size is `clamp(16px, 0.62vw + 7px, 26px)` and every menu size is in rem, so the whole interface grows with the window for TV distance. Labels, hints, pills, tags, metadata and small buttons are 1rem or larger.

rules.name: The Spotlight Rule
rules.body: Nothing lifts at rest. A control rises and glows only because it has focus (keyboard, controller) or, for covers, because the pointer is on it.

dos: **Do** draw every control background as a squared slab skewed by `var(--lean)` (-9deg), with the label upright inside.
**Do** keep exactly three light roles: magenta for the forward or music-starting action, cyan for focus, a lit slab with a white 4px underline for selection.
**Do** show focus with the spotlight: 3px lift, cyan edge and ring, cyan glow, and the radial cone from above, for keyboard and controller focus alike.
**Do** move selection with one travelling lit slab per group (0.42s, --ease-out) rather than toggling each item's fill.
**Do** use lane colours only to mean lane, difficulty or multiplier level.
